haiku-low.q2: The Dispatcher fans out one delivery per matching subscription, deduped on (event_id, subscription_id). That key stops a redelivered copy of the same event creating a second delivery.
haiku-low.q3: The document says only that there is an HMAC-SHA256 signature header. What it covers, and whether it is made per delivery or per attempt, is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q4: Success marks the delivery Delivered. A 410 goes to dead letter and disables the subscription. Other permanent failures go to dead letter; transient failures retry with backoff. Which 4xx codes are permanent is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q5: Up to 8 attempts. The delay before the third attempt is NOT STATED; the document only says on the agreed schedule.
haiku-low.q6: In the deliveries table. The specific fields (status, attempt count, next due time, last result) are NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q7: NOT STATED. The document does not say where a retryable delivery waits, what triggers its next attempt, or how the 15-minute queue limit is handled.
haiku-low.q8: Workers use leases, so the work is not lost. Whether the request is resent or the result recorded is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q9: Dead deliveries are kept 14 days and can be replayed via the Admin API. Where they are held is NOT STATED, and what a replay changes is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q10: The webhook id header lets receivers dedupe. Whether that value changes between retries or after a replay is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: The document says only that disabled subscriptions are handled. What happens to waiting deliveries is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. The document does not discuss ordering of events.

sonnet.q1: A "domain-events" stream feeds the Dispatcher, which starts the work. The document doesn't say which existing component produces the events, so that part is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q2: The Dispatcher fans an event out to matching subscriptions, one delivery per subscription. It dedupes on (event_id, subscription_id), so a redelivered event message can't create a second delivery.
sonnet.q3: NOT STATED. The document only says there is an HMAC-SHA256 signature header. It doesn't say what the signature covers or whether it is made once or per attempt.
sonnet.q4: Success goes to Delivered. A 410 is a permanent failure: it goes straight to dead letter and disables the subscription. Other permanent failures go straight to dead letter, but the document doesn't say which 4xx codes count as permanent. Transient failures retry with backoff.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts. The delay before the third attempt is NOT STATED: the document says only "the agreed schedule" and doesn't give it.
sonnet.q6: The `deliveries` table holds the deliveries. The document doesn't name columns for status, attempt count, next-due time or last result, so those are NOT STATED.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED. The document doesn't say where a retry waits, what triggers it, or anything about a queue or its 15-minute delay limit. It says only "Retry with backoff" and that workers use leases.
sonnet.q8: The document says only that workers use leases so a crash doesn't lose work. It doesn't say what happens in this case, such as a re-send. Receivers can dedupe using the webhook id header.
sonnet.q9: Dead deliveries are in the `deliveries` table, which the cleanup job also acts on. They are kept 14 days. They can be listed and replayed through the Admin API. What a replay changes is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q10: The webhook id header lets receivers dedupe. Whether it stays the same across retries or after a replay is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document says only "Disabled subscriptions are handled" and that a 410 disables the subscription.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. The document doesn't mention ordering guarantees.
